upkeep.title: Upkeep — Agent That Keeps Your Pull Requests Mergeable
upkeep.description: Upkeep keeps a repository's pull requests mergeable. It looks at the whole queue of open PRs, plans the order they can merge in, fixes what a bounded policy allows, proves every fix with the compiler and the tests, remembers the fixes that passed and hands the rest back with a diagnosis and a receipt of what each model did and cost. It runs on NVIDIA Nemotron models (Ultra, Super and Nano) served by Nebius Token Factory, reads migration guides found with Tavily and ships as one Go binary with its dashboard built in. On upkeep-sample, a notes service with nine PRs built to show one blocker each, the whole run costs about two cents ($0.0191 against $0.0502 at the largest model's price for the same tokens), and five live runs against the real models ended with all 45 PRs as the scenario expects.

meta.platform: CLI + web dashboard (single binary), GitHub Action

items.description: Before touching code it finds which PRs change the same files and which would conflict (git merge-tree), and suggests a merge order
Merges the base branch into a scratch copy and runs build, vet and tests in a container without network; the first failure is the blocker
For dependency upgrades it searches the migration guide with Tavily, predicts what will break and later marks each prediction confirmed or not seen by the build
Merges and formatting are mechanical; small conflicts go to Ultra in one call; broken builds and tests go to Super, with four tools and up to three clean attempts
A checklist outside the model decides: build, vet and tests green, at most 5 files and 80 lines, no test touched, Go only and no new comments
A fix that passed the verifier is reapplied with no model call when the same failure comes back; on the second run the cost dropped from $0.0191 to $0.0055
Never force-pushes, never merges a PR opened by a person and never lets a fix edit, delete or skip tests; these are rules in code, not in a prompt

logiops-ai.title: LogiOps AI — Operations Desk with an Agent and MCP
logiops-ai.description: LogiOps AI is an operations desk you talk to, on a simulated Alexa+ device over a real self-hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, spec 2025-11-25, with an Agent Skill and MCP Apps). Ask about a late shipment: an agent reads the orders, stock and carrier quotes through MCP tools, code prices every feasible plan and the agent recommends one. You approve with one "yes"; the system executes the plan once and verifies the result. Measured on the deployed demo with live Amazon Bedrock: question to grounded recommendation in 12.2 s with 5 MCP calls, for about US$0.04 of Bedrock usage. The design principle: the agent proposes, you approve, code enforces it.

meta.platform: Web (simulated device + operator console), MCP server, AWS

items.description: The agent (Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock) reads the incident through MCP tools; deterministic code calculates every feasible plan and the agent picks one by cost, arrival time and order priority
Every answer, the spoken line included, is checked against the incident's data before it is shown
No tool can approve: an approval names the exact plan and data version, and a data change invalidates it and raises a proactive alert
Execution is idempotent and verified; a booking reads its price back and is charged once, with a receipt
A rule, a spend cap and a note steer the pick through fixed rules, and a signed-in person is welcomed back in the next session
/demo, the simulated Alexa+ device with voice and the plans as an MCP App, and /console, the operator console; both share one backend

pusaq.title: Pusaq — Model Gateway with Quotas and Cost Accounting
pusaq.description: Pusaq is a Go gateway for an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions subset. Your app points at its endpoint, picks a model alias and Pusaq handles access, limits and provider fallback. Redis holds quotas and monthly spend with atomic operations, configuration is validated at startup and every request emits a JSON cost event. The repository ships reproducible measurement reports with their protocol, environment and limits: limiter exactness, circuit-breaker detection, a 204-row labeled corpus for the content rules and regional failover. The scope is deliberate: no tool calling or structured outputs, and the semantic cache runs in shadow mode, measuring without ever serving responses.

items.description: Configurable aliases (pusaq/fast, pusaq/best, pusaq/auto), feature rules, circuit breakers and provider fallback
API keys, per-model permissions and monthly spending limits
Request and token buckets with atomic Redis operations, in strict or leased mode
Buffered and SSE responses, token usage and JSON cost events with the price-table version
Content heuristics and a semantic cache in shadow mode
Dated reports with protocol and limits, and recipes to reproduce them (make loadtest, make tpmtest, make breakertest)

onesqlx.title: OneSQLx — SQL-First Analytics Platform
onesqlx.description: OneSQLx is an open source analytics platform built with Elixir and Phoenix LiveView, aimed at teams who would rather write SQL than fight a visual query builder. It connects external PostgreSQL databases with encrypted credentials (AES-256-GCM), syncs the catalog through pg_catalog to power autocomplete, and executes queries with read-only enforced at the session level. On top of that sit saved query collections, dashboards with cross-filtering and public sharing, scheduled reports with alerts, data lineage, an audit trail and a versioned REST API with scoped tokens.

items.description: Connect external PostgreSQL with encrypted credentials (AES-256-GCM), SSL support and read-only enforced per session
Automatic schema, table and column introspection via pg_catalog, synced in the background with Oban
CodeMirror 6 with catalog-driven autocomplete, a guard that blocks writes, named parameters, EXPLAIN ANALYZE and query cancellation
KPI, table, bar, line, pie, area and scatter cards with Chart.js, cross-filtering, presentation mode and revocable public links
5-field cron on top of Oban, conditional alerts on results and notification via email or webhook
Workspaces with roles, dashboard → query → table lineage, audit trail and usage analytics
Versioned under /api/v1 with scoped tokens (read/execute/manage), rate limiting, OpenAPI 3 spec and Swagger UI

lynix.title: Lynix — API Testing CLI for CI/CD
lynix.description: Lynix is a Go CLI for declarative API testing in CI/CD pipelines. HTTP requests are defined in version-controlled YAML collections, run against different environments, and validated with assertions on status, latency, JSONPath, and JSON Schema. It follows hexagonal architecture (domain, ports, use cases, adapters), redacts sensitive data before storing run artifacts, and generates JUnit XML reports ready for any pipeline.

items.description: HTTP requests defined in version-controlled YAML, no code required
Status, latency, JSONPath, and JSON Schema validation
Extract values from one response to use in the next request
JSON output, JUnit XML reports, and pipeline-ready exit codes
Masks headers, tokens, and secrets before saving run artifacts
Converts curl commands or Postman collections into Lynix collections
